meta.title: How it works | Keepsite Media
meta.description: Three stages, three decisions, one round of changes at each. What building a site with Keepsite looks like, how long it takes, and what we need from you.

heading: How it works
lead: You've already made the decision to hand this off. What's left is three decisions, and we bring you each one when it's ready.
timeline: Most sites launch four to six weeks after kickoff. The biggest variable is how quickly you reply at each stage.

steps.title: Tell us about your business.
steps.body: Eight questions, most of which you can answer off the top of your head. On Growth, Agile and Range there's a kickoff call too, so we hear it in your words.

steps.title: Pick a direction.
steps.body: We send you one page with four different home page designs on it. You pick the one that looks like your business, then answer two short questionnaires: one on your brand, one to drive the build. From Growth up, research into what your customers search for runs at the same time and shapes what comes next.

steps.title: We lay out every page.
steps.body: You see every page the site will have and how each one is put together. The words and photos come later.

steps.title: We add the words and photos.
steps.body: Your copy on Presence, ours from Growth up. You look it over, send your changes in one go, and we launch.

steps.title: We keep it working.
steps.body: Hosting, maintenance, monitoring, and a summary every quarter. From Growth up, we keep watching search and adjusting. On Agile, we keep meeting.

meetings.heading: How often we talk
meetings.lead: No standing meetings on Presence. The others get exactly the ones the work needs.

items.name: Presence
items.body: None scheduled. Everything runs on the questionnaires and email.

items.name: Growth
items.body: A kickoff call, and a check-in at each stage.

items.name: Agile
items.body: A kickoff, a check-in every two weeks during the build, and a strategy meeting every month after launch.

items.name: Range
items.body: A kickoff call, and a check-in at each stage.

stages.heading: The three stages
stages.lead: Each stage settles one question before the next one starts.

items.label: Stage 1
items.title: Style
items.see: One page you scroll through, with four different home page designs on it. It's there to show you a look, not a finished site: nothing on it is wired up, and none of it is about your business yet.
items.decide: Which one looks like your business.
items.note: You're picking a direction, not a final design. From there we fit it to your business, your colors, your photos.

tiers.name: Presence
tiers.body: Pick a direction and this stage is done.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.body: While you're choosing, we're studying the search results you want to win. By stage two we know which pages you need.

tiers.name: Agile
tiers.body: We start with longer discovery about where the business is going, then research where the obvious data doesn't exist. The search strategy gets invented here.

tiers.name: Range
tiers.body: The same research as Growth, run for every arm of the business.

terms.body: The plan for which searches your site should show up for, and which pages will do it. Growth, Agile and Range only.

items.label: Stage 2
items.title: Function
items.see: A layout for every page the site will have. Image areas are outlined boxes and the text is lorem ipsum, the standard placeholder.
items.decide: Whether the site has every page you need.
items.note: The placeholder text is on purpose. If we filled it in with real words, you'd read them instead of looking at the page, and they aren't written yet.

tiers.name: Presence
tiers.body: The pages you asked for, in the order that makes sense for them.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.body: The page list comes out of the research, so there are usually service or location pages you hadn't thought to ask for.

tiers.name: Agile
tiers.body: More research shapes each page, and the site is built so the strategy can be swapped later without breaking what works.

tiers.name: Range
tiers.body: One section per arm, structured so the arms don't compete with each other on Google.

terms.body: The shape of a page: what goes where, and in what order. The floor plan before the furniture.

items.label: Stage 3
items.title: Copy and photos
items.see: The finished site, with the words and images in place.
items.decide: That it's ready to go live.
items.note: Your photos, and your copy if you're on Presence, are due before this stage starts. After that it's one last look, then we launch.

tiers.name: Presence
tiers.body: You send us your words. We edit them and put them in place.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.body: We write your core pages around the research. There's one call first, so we get your tone right.

tiers.name: Agile
tiers.body: The same call and the same writing, plus an A/B test where there's a real question to answer.

tiers.name: Range
tiers.body: The same writing, for every arm.

terms.body: The words on your website. Headlines, page text, button labels, all of it. Nothing to do with copying anything.
Two versions of a page shown to different visitors, so the numbers decide which one stays.

end.label: Launch
end.title: Your site goes live.
end.body: That was the last decision. From here the site is ours to keep running, with hosting, maintenance, and monitoring on every package.

tiers.name: Presence
tiers.body: Hosting, maintenance, monitoring, one change a month, and a plain-English summary every quarter.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.body: All of that, plus search monitoring and updates tied to your search goals.

tiers.name: Agile
tiers.body: All of that, plus a strategy meeting every month, ongoing research, and tests.

tiers.name: Range
tiers.body: Growth's after-launch work, for every arm.

terms.body: We watch the site for outages, broken pages, and errors, so problems get caught before you notice them.

changes.heading: One round of changes at every stage.
changes.body: Changes cost the least while the site is still rough, so that's where we put them. If none of the four directions works, we show you more. If a page is laid out wrong, we redo it while it's still empty. The last round is for the finished site, once the words and photos are in.

needFromYou.heading: What we need from you
items: Accurate information about your business: what you do, where, for whom, your hours, and anything a customer would ask.
A pick from the four directions we show you at stage one.
Your photos and logo, and your copy if you're on Presence, by the start of stage three.
A reply at each stage. On Growth, Agile and Range, the calls listed above.

wontHaveTo.heading: What you won't have to do
items: No blank page to stare at.
No switching off the tools you already use.
No decisions about hosting, plugins, or platforms.

closing.heading: Keep your business moving.
closing.sub: We'll take care of the website.
